1oe1bzb:232: The biggest cognitive trap in full-stack SDD development is treating AI as an "idea generator". The essence of Dewu's experience is: give AI an existing implementation as a reference and let it replicate a copy accordingly. From an engineering perspective, this means you need to actively find the most similar existing implementation in the codebase and explicitly specify reference files, API paths, and data structures in the prompt. This "constrained navigation" approach shifts the quality of AI generation from "depending on luck" to "depending on context density". The more precise the constraints, the higher the adoption rate of the generated code and the lower the review cost—which directly explains why code generated out of thin air is often largely rejected during Code Review.
1olejxy:229: A complete R&D iteration is abstracted as a PDCA cycle (Plan: requirement alignment / Do: development implementation / Check: effect verification / Act: analysis and reflection). Most teams' AI practice is concentrated on writing code in the Do phase; Dewu wants AI to enter the entire cycle. The four prerequisites for full-chain AI adoption: Plan: clear requirements (goals and boundaries do not waver), Do: fewer interruptions (AI executes continuously without frequent questioning), Check: quantified results (the black box is judged by test results plus post-hoc data), Act: experience reuse (past pitfalls are not repeated). The goal is to increase AI penetration and adoption rates and shorten iteration cycles (biweekly → weekly, weekly → daily).
